brief: A steel flange disc 60 mm across and 8 mm thick. A 20 mm bore runs all the way through the centre. Two 6 mm bolt holes pass all the way through the disc, 40 mm apart. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

implied: The disc has a flat mounting face.
stated: A steel flange disc 60 mm across and 8 mm thick.
A 20 mm bore runs all the way through the center.
Two 6 mm bolt holes pass all the way through the disc, 40 mm apart.
intent.summary: A steel flange disc with a 60 mm diameter and 8 mm thickness. It has a 20 mm bore running through the center and two 6 mm bolt holes, 40 mm apart. The disc carries no load.
unstated: The magnitude and direction of the load on the arm.

note: requirements: the record as the run accepted it, Forge's additions included. The answer is the design the run built after three designer attempts: a disc and a bore, both bolt-hole parameters declared and read by nothing, no bolt hole drawn.

notes: dropped 1 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about

added REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_X and REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_Y at 60 mm: the brief calls the part square or round at its largest stated size, and nothing in the requirement set measured the part's size at all. A dimension parameter is declared just as truthfully by a plate 30 by 12 as by a plate 30 by 30, and one was: sixteen claims, every one green, and the plate was 30 by 12.

added REQ_ROUND: the brief calls this part round, and two equal bounding boxes do not say a part is round -- a 25 mm square block has a 25 by 25 box exactly as a 25 mm cylinder does. One run asked for a shaft collar and got a square block with both extent claims passing. This measures the built surface: 1 is a cylinder, a square is 0.707.

added REQ_HOLES_20MM_ON_AXIS: the brief states 1 open hole of 20 mm down the part's axis, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_6MM: the brief states 2 open holes of 6 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.
